prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Cross-tab · Regional sales (language en).
Grid: 7 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Region" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 195px
  col 2: header "Jan" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 3: header "Feb" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 4: header "Mar" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 5: header "Apr" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 6: header "May" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 7: header "Jun" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 490px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 489px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare monthly sales across regions from January through June.","reading":"Readers scan across each row to follow a region over time and down each month to compare regions.","groups":["January–June are parallel monthly measures and should have consistent widths.","The region column identifies each row and needs enough space for recognizable labels."],"keep_intact":["Month names","Sales figures, including thousands separators","Individual words in region names"],"may_wrap":["Multiword region names may wrap at spaces; the long Europe, Middle East & Africa label is the main candidate."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [133, 59, 59, 59, 59, 59, 59] · table 488×206px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [127, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60] · table 488×206px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
